hooks.text: One supergiant galaxy almost bridges the Milky Way and Andromeda.
IC 1101 spans an astonishing 1.7 million light-years in diameter.
Astronomers discovered a colossal cosmic monster hiding in plain sight.

title: The Cosmic Colossus That Baffles Astronomers
description: Discover IC 1101, a supergiant galaxy so vast it would almost bridge the gap between the Milky Way and Andromeda.

beats.text: One supergiant galaxy almost bridges the Milky Way and Andromeda.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of galaxy cluster Abell 2029

beats.text: On June 19, 1790, astronomer William Herschel discovered this faint celestial smudge in the constellation Virgo.
beats.visual: Portrait of astronomer Sir William Herschel

beats.text: Today, we know that smudge as IC 1101, anchored at the center of the Abell 2029 galaxy cluster.
beats.visual: Abell 2029 galaxy cluster image by Hubble Space Telescope

beats.text: Recent ultra-deep observations using the Isaac Newton Telescope revealed its measured main body spans 1.7 million light-years.
beats.visual: Isaac Newton Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory
queries: Isaac Newton Telescope Roque de los Muchachos

beats.text: Containing trillions of solar masses, this cosmic colossus grew into a monster by cannibalizing neighboring galaxies.
beats.visual: Artist concept of galactic cannibalism and galaxy mergers

beats.text: Faint plume-like outer remnants show that it is still actively devouring nearby galactic debris today.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory observation of Abell 2029 cluster

beats.text: That is why this supergiant galaxy is so massive it would almost bridge the Milky Way and Andromeda.
beats.visual: Milky Way Galaxy structure and disk visualization
queries: Milky Way Galaxy artist concept NASA
